items.pregunta: Is every token the change accepts (JWT, ID token, signed cookie) verified with a server-chosen algorithm and key, and checked for expiry, and for issuer and audience when the key or issuer is shared with other services, before any of its claims are used?
items.evidencia: The verify call with its algorithm, key and claim options, and no path that decodes the token without verifying it

items.pregunta: Does the OAuth, OIDC or SAML callback accept only a response bound to the session that started the flow (state or nonce checked, signed assertion is the one used), so a response started by someone else is refused?
items.evidencia: The comparison of state, nonce or the signed element against what the session stored

items.pregunta: Does every state-changing route authenticated by a cookie refuse a cross-site request (anti-CSRF token, SameSite=Lax or Strict on that cookie, or an exact Origin check)?
items.evidencia: The CSRF middleware or Origin check on the route, or the SameSite=Lax or Strict attribute where the session cookie is set; bearer-only routes do not need it

items.pregunta: Do password reset, MFA enrolment or removal, and email or phone change require the current factor or a single-use, expiring token bound to that account and that action, with the reset or verification link built from a configured base URL and not from the request Host header?
items.evidencia: Token generation and consumption (expiry, one-time use, account binding), the re-authentication check before the change, and the base URL of the link

items.pregunta: Is an API key resolved to its server-side record, with the tenant, scopes and environment taken from that record and never from request parameters?
items.evidencia: The key lookup and where the tenant and scopes used by the handler come from

items.pregunta: Is the session identifier replaced at login and at a privilege change, and revoked on the server at logout and password change, so an earlier or copied identifier stops working?
items.evidencia: The regenerate, rotate or revoke calls on the login, logout and password-change paths
